items.title: Alvin "Red" Tyler Interview, 1996-06-19
items.q: Otis Ducker had the band there. And it, Melvin Lasty, uh, August DuPont, June Gardner, and several other guys.

ctx.x: The only problem was that we got stranded in, and, uh, Port Arthur, Texas. Stranded. I forgot who all was on the band. Um, it might have been, uh, uh, Lil' Dime, DuPont. August DuPont, yeah. Yeah, he, I think he might have been on it and some other guys. I don't, I can't remember, but we got stranded. And how we got home was that, uh, Earl Barnes got in touch with him and he was a Mason and he had the Masons to pay for the bus to get us back to New Orleans. He gets back home, yeah. You know. And, uh, that was one…
And, uh, uh, uh, so, yes, uh, did, uh, were you ever, did, did, did, did the Dew Drop, shows like the Dew Drop pay very well?

items.title: Albert "June" Gardner Interview, 1996-04-17
items.q: We used to work so much with just regular guys like Ray Tyler, Chuck, Eddie Collins, myself. We would have nine jobs in a week.

ctx.x: Or somebody who could play modern jazz, but you told them to play a blues?

Yeah, like a lot of these low rhythm and blues band, they had riffs that they would play. I mean Roy Brown had riff riff riff. Yeah, you know, that, that, da, da, da, da, da, da, you know. Right. It's simple, you know, if you start, play this, you know. Right. But uh, well, most overall it was a good band because like during those times we would play maybe an hour or so before he would even come on and sing. Oh, okay. So people would be dancing and the band is hot and hitting. It was, and we'd been together for a…
